key_insight: Reframe motion-controlled image-to-video generation as a two-stage reasoning-then-generation problem so the system infers missing causal consequences of sparse/imprecise user trajectories before synthesizing video, yielding more natural and commonsense-consistent motion.
problem_solved: Existing motion-conditioned video models rigidly follow sparse or imprecise user trajectories and therefore produce unnatural or implausible outcomes by missing secondary causal effects and commonsense interactions.
method: Learn a visual-reasoning module that takes a static image + sparse trajectory and predicts completed motion, secondary causal outcomes, and commonsense constraints.
Feed the reasoning output into a motion-conditioned video generator to synthesize temporally coherent frames that respect both user intent and inferred causal consequences.
Train end-to-end with objectives that align reasoning and generation (e.g., reconstruction, perceptual/consistency losses and commonsense/causal regularizers) to reduce implausible artifacts.
impact: Enables practitioners to produce more realistic, controllable videos from minimal motion inputs and reduces failure modes caused by imprecise guidance—useful for animation, AR/VR, and content creation pipelines where natural interactions and secondary effects matter.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: 'Input image + sparse trajectory' → 'Visual reasoning (trajectory completion + causal inference)' → 'Motion-conditioned video generator' → 'Output video'.
Before/after examples: left column shows rigid-following artifacts from sparse input; right column shows corrected, commonsense-consistent outputs from MotiMotion.
Causal-flow overlay: simple graph or arrows showing primary motion and inferred secondary effects (e.g., object collision, cloth/tail/secondary motion).
Motion field / optical-flow visualization and attention maps to illustrate where the model infers additional motion and why.
paper_title: MotiMotion: Motion-Controlled Video Generation with Visual Reasoning
paper_authors: Lee Hsin-Ying, Hanwen Jiang, Yiqun Mei, Jing Shi, Ming-Hsuan Yang
